content.title: These Haircuts Are Going To Be Huge For Spring 2026
content.text: If the past couple seasons have been focused on embracing natural texture and no-fuss hairstyles, spring 2026 is gearing up to be all that and a little something extra. Kicking off a new season calls for fresh starts of all kinds, making it the perfect time for spring 2026 hair trends to guide us straight to the salon for a new haircut or hair color. Because it's never too late to switch up your look this year! Low-maintenance styling is being taken up a notch with statement-making cuts that do all the work and call back to past eras and decades. If you've been wanting to make a chop, there are shaggy layers, blunt fringe, and retro styles just waiting to be shorn. We're talking modern updates on vintage bobs, bangs, and long cuts, too. Here are the trendy haircuts you'll be seeing everywhere for spring 2026. Textured Layers Credit: @chrisjones_hair You can add so much more texture to naturally fine hair using layers, layers, and more layers—focusing midway down the hair to the ends ensures you don't lose too much volume. Short and Wild Shag Credit: @salsalhair Nothing flatters a head full of curls like a classic shag. It's definitely the cool girl cut of the bunch. Blunt Collarbone Cut Credit: @hairby_chrissy⁠⠀ A lob that hits right at your collarbone seems to be sworn in as the most flattering length this year. Soft Curved Bob Credit: @lucyhale We're taking things back to the Old Hollywood bobs of yesteryear—which means soft ends, flattering curves, and a deep side part. Wispy Bangs Credit: @natalieannehair / Instagram In case you got distracted by the show-stopping ginger hair color, this cut deserves just as much attention. Curls love a bunch of layering to add to their natural bounce, and wispy bangs refresh absolutely any haircut or length. Cheekbone-Grazing 90s Bob Credit: @hirohair This chic little number isn't going anywhere. It's all about razor-sharp lines and super glossy strands. Mia Wallace Bob Credit: @bobbyeliot This Pulp Fiction cut is iconic in its own right, but it fits in just as well today. Mini Blunt Bob Credit: @chrisjones_hair Just because you go blunt, it doesn't mean you have to sacrifice texture. This mini bob that grazes the chin has the best of both worlds. Blunt Textured Cut Credit: @riawna Instantly make your hair look thicker by leaving the ends blunt and putting textured bend into the body. Curtain Bangs Credit: @studiolioness Perhaps our favorite trend that's been gaining steam, curtain bangs look super stylish and a little bit retro all at the same time. Short Shag Cut Credit: @salsalhair Curls are full of body, and a chin-length cut with bangs is a flattering and unique choice, seen here by stylist Sal Salcedo. Sharp Shoulder Cut Credit: @natalieannehair This style could cut glass with just one look, and it makes any classic bob or lob look modern and on-trend. 1970s Long Cut Credit: @los_pastel The soft, feathered, and fluffy looks of the 1970s are not to be forgotten. This modern long cut gives a nod to the long-haired babes of decades past. Lob-Length Curls Credit: @jesseniaspallet It'd be hard not to get an instant confidence boost from this medium-length curly cut with layers and very subtle curtain bangs. Choppy Layers Credit: @marisacuts Give your haircut an edgy dose of cool with choppy layers and bangs. It makes a plain lob look so last year. Curly Pixie Cut Credit: @t.techniques Add a side part to a cropped cut for extra volume, which curls already enhance naturally. Blunt Chin Bob Credit: @marisacuts We wish we could speak our minds as bluntly as these ends. Keeping a cut free from too much layering ensures a super thick bob with tons of style. Barely-There Bangs Credit: @natalieannehair Curls make wispy bangs even more perfectly haphazard, especially when paired with short layers. Textured Fringe Bob Credit: @chrisjones_hair A take on a classic shag, this short bob by stylist Chris Jones plays up all the texture with layers and thick curtain bangs. Textured Lob Credit: @donovanmillshair Keeping your haircut mainly one-length without too many layers will always make it look enviously thick. This lob cut is roll-out-of-bed ready to go at all times. Fringed Short Curls Credit: @biancacolour Layers can give so much life to curls, and that especially goes for short cuts. Add lots of layers and a voluminous set of bangs, and you're set to steal envious looks everywhere you go. Trim Pixie Credit: @veronica_nunez/Instagram When you're ready to take the ultimate plunge, call this pixie á la Mia Farrow up. It'll do the job—and more. Layered Mid-Length Cut Credit: @natalieannehair This is the definition of letting your hair color do the work. Easy layers and a versatile length mean that you won't be labored down with styling time. Thick Balayaged Curls Credit: @leysahairandmakeup Letting curls grow and run as they may is easy with a good haircut. Here, layers and bangs only add to natural volume. Soft A-Line Bob Credit: @hirohair This low-maintenance cut is slightly longer in the front than the back, which elongates and flatters oval and round face shapes to no end. Long and Layered Cut Credit: @donovanmillshair You thought you'd seen the last of this early-to-mid 2000s cut, hm? When everyone else is going short, why not go long? Big Shoulder-Grazing Curls Credit: @natalieannehair This length is not to be ignored. It's short enough to really snatch onto major volume and long enough to make a statement. Curly Side-Parted Bob Credit: @curlsbyjessw For those who like a short cut, this short bob from Curls By Jess gets style from a side part and side-swept bangs. Grown-Out Crop This might be the most elegant crop cut we've seen all year. Side-swept bangs and flattering layers keep it wearable and long. Cropped Bangs Credit: @salsalhair Baby bangs are here to stay. It's the perfect accessory to a loud long cut of curls. Retro Pixie Cut Credit: @hairbyuno This feels vintage in the best way. An icy blonde hair color paired with a sassy short cut is a match made in the salon. Early 2000s Sideswept Bangs Credit: @los_pastel That's right: You get a second chance to do sideswept bangs—correctly this time 'round. Thick Curly Cut Credit: @leysahairandmakeup Curls don't have to be weighed down, even if they are enviously thick. Ask for layering and wispy bangs to gradually add volume. Angled Long Bob Credit: @chrisjones_hair Angles are a great way to refresh any length, especially short cuts that fall above the collarbones. Ask for an A-line cut that's longer in the front, but not stacked in the back. The New Triangle Cut Credit: @sarahkstylistmt Curly girls are taught to be afraid of ending up with a triangle cut (also known as the pyramid cut), but this modern version is changing the tune. Flippy Layers Credit: @lindseyneavitt901 Flippy layers have a nostalgic, early-2000s feel, but that's not the only reason to order them up at the salon. They also make it easier to mock the look of a fresh, bouncy blowout. Curly Super Pixie Credit: Christina Kelley / @msberrybacon Leaving your curls long on top gives so much life and volume to a short cropped cut. Shaggy Shoulder Cut Credit: @hairby_chrissy Give that classic shoulder cut an edgy finish by asking for shag-inspired layers and curtain bangs. It's ideal for those who want extra volume and texture. Curly Fringe Credit: @sarahcurlboss For those looking to add something new to a bob-length cut, bangs are an easy fix. You can go as wispy or full as you'd like. Tousled Medium-Length Cut Credit: @slim_color For thick-haired woman who don't want to go too short, layers are going to be your best bet. Add side-swept bangs for an extra textured look. Curly Crop Cut Credit: @leysahairandmakeup There's no problem that a big chop and fresh hair color can't fix. Don't be afraid to go shorter! Angled Long Lob Credit: @styled_by_carolynn Angled cuts are the perfect way to add a bit of interest to a short cut. You can take it anywhere from chin-length to a long bob, as seen here. Shaggy Curly Bangs Credit: @veronica_nunez Wispy bangs are so flattering on curly hair and work seamlessly into any face-framing layers you might have—which with curls, layers are always the way to go! Breezy Lob Length Credit: @chrisjones_hair This year is all about low-maintenance cuts, and this one is the perfect example while still adding a bit of volume and texture to more fine hair. Extra Stacked Bob Credit: @styled_by_carolynn For those with thick hair, it might seem daunting to ask for a stacked or angled cut, but you can really make the most of these volume-packed cuts. Frequently Asked Questions There are many trending haircuts to try this season, depending highly on your ideal length, natural texture, and style preference. Long bobs are one of the most asked-for lengths, while short hairstyles overall are leading the pack. While this is dependent on your texture and thickness, bobs continue to be the most requested length. Ask for a length between your chin and shoulders for a low-maintenance and versatile look. Generally, shorter hairstyles above the shoulders are most recommended for women over 50, as it helps maintain your hair health and promotes thicker-looking results.
